metaTitle: Best MagSafe Power Banks for iPhone
metaDescription: Compare six MagSafe-compatible power banks by Qi2 wireless speed, capacity, thickness, cooling and built-in cable, with honest notes on real iPhone charging.
expertTake: The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is the top pick for the fastest magnetic charging, with a stated 25 W Qi2.2 pad and an active cooling fan. The Enyneo 10,000 mAh Qi2 bank is the value pick when you want the standard at the lowest place in the price order. Skip the category if you only charge with a cable, because a plain USB-C power bank gives more capacity and speed for the same money.
introParagraphs: A MagSafe-style power bank snaps onto the back of an iPhone with magnets and charges wirelessly, so there is no cable to carry or plug in. The newer Qi2 standard standardises the magnet ring and allows up to 15 W of wireless power, which makes the format practical rather than a novelty.

The tradeoffs are real: wireless charging is slower and warmer than a cable, thick banks make the phone awkward to hold and the magnet strength varies. This guide compares capacity, wireless speed, thickness, cooling and extras so you can pick the right balance.

products.name: Anker MagGo 2 Pro 10,000 mAh Qi2.2 25W Magnetic Power Bank
products.description:
The MagGo 2 Pro is the fastest model here, built around a Qi2.2 pad rated for up to 25 W of wireless charging, which the maker says rivals wired speed on a compatible phone. A small fan, two air channels and three graphene layers manage heat, which is the main limit on fast wireless charging. The 45 W USB-C port recharges the bank itself to 80 percent in a stated 52 minutes.

The tradeoff is that it is the highest in the price order of the eight candidates we reviewed, and the 25 W figure only applies to a phone that supports the Qi2.2 speed. An older iPhone still charges at the slower rate. Compared with the 15 W MagGo at 10,000 mAh, you pay for the cooling fan and the faster recharge, which a casual user may not need.

In ownership, the fan is the part to watch: dust can collect in the air channels, and a fan is a moving part that can wear. Keep the vents clear, avoid pocketing the bank while it charges and remember that a case that is too thick weakens the magnets. It is the right choice for someone who charges every day.
products.bestFor: People who want the fastest magnetic charge and are willing to pay for active cooling.
pros: Qi2.2 pad rated up to 25 W gives the fastest wireless speed in the lineup
Active fan and graphene layers manage heat during fast charging
45 W USB-C recharge brings the bank to 80% in a stated 52 minutes
10,000 mAh covers roughly one to two phone charges in a day
cons: Highest in the price order among all eight candidates here
Full 25 W speed needs a compatible phone, so older iPhones charge slower

products.name: Anker MagGo 10,000 mAh Qi2 15W Power Bank with Smart Display
products.description:
The MagGo 10,000 mAh is the Qi2-certified 15 W workhorse with a smart display that shows the battery level and the time left to a full recharge. Certification means the magnet ring, power negotiation and temperature controls follow the Qi2 specification instead of a maker's own design. A display is handy because most magnetic banks only show a few LED dots.

The tradeoff is that 15 W is slower than the 25 W MagGo 2 Pro, and it is among the higher models in the price order. It has no fan, so it relies on passive cooling and slows if it heats. Compared with the Zolo, which tops out at 7.5 W wireless, the MagGo doubles the speed but costs more.

Ownership is mostly about heat and the display. Keep the phone out of direct sun while charging and let the bank cool between back-to-back sessions. The display is a battery drain of its own, so charge it before a long day instead of relying on it as a last-minute backup.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a certified 15 W bank with a readable battery display.
pros: Qi2 certification means the magnet and power rules follow the standard
Display shows percentage and time to full, which beats a few LED dots
15 W wireless doubles the old 7.5 W rate on a compatible iPhone
10,000 mAh gives a phone one to two full charges away from a wall
cons: No cooling fan, so heavy use warms the pack and slows charging
Costs more than the Zolo and Enyneo for the display and certified speed

products.name: Anker Nano 5,000 mAh Qi2 15W Magnetic Power Bank, 0.3 in
products.description:
The Nano trades capacity for thinness. At about 0.3 inches thick it adds little bulk to an iPhone, and the 5,000 mAh cell is enough for roughly one top-up on a modern phone. It is Qi2 certified at up to 15 W and lists temperature monitoring, which is the safety point to look for on a slim pack.

The tradeoff is that the battery is half the size of the 10,000 mAh models, so it is a pocket backup, not a day-long power source. A phone with a large battery may only gain about a half to one full charge. Against the MagGo 10,000 mAh, you give up capacity and the display for a pack that can stay on the phone all day without making it unwieldy.

In ownership, a slim bank warms faster than a thicker one, so avoid charging in a pocket or under a blanket. The magnets also hold less well through a thick case. Recharge it over USB-C overnight, and keep it away from cards and hotel key cards if you use a wallet on the phone.
products.bestFor: Commuters who want a thin pack that lives on the phone and gives one quick top-up.
pros: At about 0.3 inches thick it barely changes how the phone feels
Qi2 certified at up to 15 W, so it matches the larger MagGo on speed
Temperature control is stated, which matters most on a thin pack
Lighter than the 10,000 mAh models in a small bag or pocket
cons: 5,000 mAh is about half a day of heavy phone use for many people
Slim cell warms faster under load, so fast charging can taper

products.name: Anker Zolo 10,000 mAh Magnetic Power Bank with Stand and Cable
products.description:
The Zolo is the practical, flexible option: a 10,000 mAh bank with a built-in cable rated for 30 W wired output and a magnetic pad that charges wirelessly at up to 7.5 W. A kickstand lets you prop the phone for video at several angles. It weighs 8.46 ounces and measures 4.15 by 2.72 by 0.81 inches, which is a regular, pocketable size.

The tradeoff is wireless speed: 7.5 W is the older, slower magnetic rate, so the cable is the way to charge quickly. Compared with the MagGo 10,000 mAh at 15 W it is slower wirelessly, and compared with the Eissix 12,000 mAh it is a smaller battery with a more established brand. It is the better choice if you will often use the cable or the stand.

In ownership, the built-in cable is the weak point on any bank: it can fray at the bend, and if it fails the bank is hurt. Wrap it loosely and avoid yanking it. The stand hinge is also a wear item, so do not lean on it hard, and keep the silicone surface clean from lint.
products.bestFor: Travellers who want a stand, a built-in cable and decent capacity in one pack.
pros: Kickstand props the phone for video calls, maps and streaming
Built-in 30 W cable avoids carrying a separate lead for wired charging
10,000 mAh at 8.46 oz is a balanced size for a daily bag
Soft silicone surface grips the phone and resists scratching it
cons: Wireless speed of up to 7.5 W is slower than Qi2 15 W models
A built-in cable can fray and cannot be replaced like a separate one

products.name: Eissix 12,000 mAh Magnetic Power Bank with 360° Stand, 22.5W
products.description:
The Eissix is the capacity leader at 12,000 mAh and sits second cheapest in the price order. It lists a strong 20N magnet, a hideable stand that rotates 360 degrees and a 22.5 W wired fast-charge port. That is a lot of battery for the money, which suits long days away from a wall socket.

The tradeoff is brand certainty. The listing does not say Qi2 certified, so wireless speed and temperature safeguards are less well documented than on the Anker models. It is also a bulkier pack than the MagGo 10,000 mAh, and the extra capacity is worth little if it makes the phone awkward. Against the Enyneo, it offers more capacity and a stand but fewer certification claims.

In ownership, test the magnet through your case and check the stand hinge for play. Avoid wireless charging in a hot car, because a larger battery can run warm. Keep a regular cable for wired top-ups, which are quicker and cooler than wireless on any pack.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want the most capacity for the money and a built-in stand.
pros: 12,000 mAh is the largest capacity in the lineup
Rotating hideable stand works in portrait and landscape
Stated 20N magnet holds the pack to the phone firmly
Second lowest in the price order, which lowers the cost of trying one
cons: No Qi2 certification stated, so wireless speed and safety are less clear
Bulkier than the MagGo 10,000 mAh, which makes the phone heavier

products.name: Enyneo 10,000 mAh Qi2 Magnetic Power Bank, PD 20W
products.description:
The Enyneo is the cheapest bank in the lineup and lists Qi2 certification, a PD 20 W USB-C port and a three-year warranty. It lists support for iPhone 12 through 17 and a 10,000 mAh cell. On paper it covers the standard that makes magnetic charging reliable, at the lowest cost.

The tradeoff is that the brand has little track record, so you rely on the warranty and the claim rather than a history. Compared with the Anker MagGo at 10,000 mAh, it has no display and fewer details about heat management. Against the Eissix it lists the Qi2 standard but has less capacity, and the warranty is the only support to lean on.

In ownership, keep the receipt and register the warranty. Check that the pack warms only modestly during a charge, and stop using it if it becomes hot or swells, as with any lithium pack. A certified bank at a low price is a fair starting point, but buy from a seller you can return it to.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want Qi2 certification and a solid warranty on a 10,000 mAh pack.
pros: Cheapest of the eight candidates, with Qi2 certification listed
Three-year warranty is longer than many in this price band
PD 20 W port covers wired charging and quick recharges
10,000 mAh gives about one to two phone charges per bank
cons: Little brand track record compared with the Anker models
No display or fan, so heat and charge status are less visible

buyingCriteria.explanation: Qi2 is the standard that fixes the magnet ring and caps wireless power at 15 W, with Qi2.2 raising it to 25 W. A certified bank such as the Anker MagGo or the Enyneo follows temperature and alignment rules, while an uncertified magnetic bank like the Eissix may charge slower. The common mistake is assuming any magnetic bank charges at 15 W.

A 10,000 mAh bank is about 37 Wh and gives a modern iPhone roughly one to two charges, less after conversion losses. The Nano at 5,000 mAh gives about one top-up, and the Eissix at 12,000 mAh gives the most. Buyers often forget that wireless charging wastes more energy as heat than a cable, so real capacity is lower.

A bank stuck to the back of a phone changes how it feels in hand. The Nano at about 0.3 inches is barely noticeable, while the Zolo at 0.81 inches and 8.46 oz is clearly heavy. Choose the thinnest pack you can live with, because a bank you leave at home gives no charge.

Wireless is convenient but slower and warmer than a cable. The MagGo 2 Pro at 25 W narrows the gap, but the Zolo at 7.5 W wireless and 30 W wired shows how large it can be. If you are in a hurry, plan to use the cable.

Wireless charging produces heat in the coil, the phone and the bank. The MagGo 2 Pro adds a fan and graphene layers to manage it, while the thinner packs rely on passive cooling. A warm phone slows its own charging, so heat management affects real speed.

The magnet ring holds the bank to the phone, and a thick or non-magnetic case weakens it. The Eissix lists a 20N magnet, a strength figure the others do not give. Check that your case is magnetic compatible, or the bank can slip off in a pocket.

specDecoder.meaning: Qi2 adds a magnet ring to wireless charging and allows up to 15 W. Qi2.2 extends the standard to 25 W on compatible phones.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the MagGo 2 Pro lists Qi2.2 at 25 W in this lineup.

specDecoder.meaning: Capacity at the cell's own voltage, which is around 3.7 V. Usable energy at the phone is about 60 to 70 percent of the headline number.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Eissix lists 12,000 mAh and the Nano 5,000 mAh, but wireless losses reduce both.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum power the magnetic pad can send, only if the phone supports it. Many phones charge slower than the maximum.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Zolo lists up to 7.5 W while the MagGo 10,000 mAh lists up to 15 W.

specDecoder.meaning: USB Power Delivery gives faster wired charging through the USB-C port. It also sets how quickly the bank recharges.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Enyneo lists 20 W, the Eissix 22.5 W and the MagGo 2 Pro 45 W.

specDecoder.meaning: A sensor that slows or stops charging when the pack gets too warm. It protects the cells and the phone.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Nano lists it, but a thin pack still warms faster than a thicker one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging standard
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each pack on Qi2 certification and stated wireless speed. The Anker MagGo and MagGo 2 Pro lead with 15 W and 25 W. The Eissix does not state certification.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacity against thickness and weight. The Nano is about 0.3 inches thick at 5,000 mAh while the Eissix reaches 12,000 mAh. We weighed bulk against use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed listing details on cooling and temperature control. The MagGo 2 Pro has a fan and the Nano lists temperature monitoring. We ranked uncertified packs lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wired performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the USB-C and cable specs, since wired charging is faster. The Zolo lists a 30 W cable and the MagGo 2 Pro a 45 W recharge. We treated all as best case.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked warranty and brand history from listings and owner feedback patterns. The Enyneo lists a three-year warranty and the Anker line has a longer track record. We lowered rank where support was unclear.

cards.label: Slim packs
cards.text: The Nano at about 0.3 inches thick and 5,000 mAh stays unobtrusive and gives one top-up. It suits commuters and light users.

cards.label: High capacity packs
cards.text: The Eissix at 12,000 mAh and the 10,000 mAh Ankers last through a day or a trip. They add thickness and weight to the phone.

howToChoose.note: Choose slim for daily convenience, and high capacity for travel days or heavy use.

rows: Thin enough to leave on the phone

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Qi2 certification, a pack compatible with your case and a wired USB-C port for faster top-ups. Check which iPhone supports Qi2.2 before paying for 25 W.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The MagGo models and the Enyneo are Qi2 certified, while the Eissix and Zolo are better treated as magnetic convenience packs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You charge daily, want 25 W wireless and cooling, or want a brand with a long record on safety.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a backup in a bag. The Enyneo or Eissix cover the basics at a low position in the price order.

maintenance.why: A lithium pack stored empty can age faster. Top it up to avoid deep discharge.
Lint and grit scratch the phone and weaken the magnet grip. A dry cloth clears them.
A built-in cable can fray at the bend. A loose port causes slow or intermittent charging.
A pack that gets hot or bulges is a safety risk. Stop using it and recycle it properly.
On the MagGo 2 Pro, dust in the air channels reduces cooling. A gentle brush keeps the airflow.

faq.q: Do MagSafe power banks charge slower than a cable?
faq.a: Yes. Wireless loses more energy as heat and charges slower than a cable. The MagGo 2 Pro narrows the gap at 25 W.

faq.q: Is a 10,000 mAh bank enough for an iPhone?
faq.a: It gives roughly one to two charges depending on the phone and wireless losses. The 5,000 mAh Nano gives about one top-up.
It is not required, but it adds standard alignment and temperature rules. Certified banks charge more predictably than uncertified ones.
A thin magnetic case works best. Thick or non-magnetic cases weaken the hold and slow charging.

faq.q: Can I take a power bank on a plane?
faq.a: Power banks go in carry-on only, and banks of 100 Wh or less are generally allowed. A 10,000 mAh bank is about 37 Wh.

faq.q: Why does my phone get warm?
faq.a: Wireless charging produces heat in both devices. If it gets hot, remove the case or use the cable.
